text:
alex: Running a short sweep this morning to understand why p99 is spiking when we enable the new kernel selector + microbatching heuristic. Observed in staging and one customer cluster in eu-west-1 after cross-region fallback test.
maria: Summary pls — is this a regression or expected tradeoff?

kevin: Short summary: avg token latency improved with kernel_opt and microbatch=4, but p99 got worse in traces where KV cache misses happen and when requests get routed cross-region during capacity pressure.

jordan: I captured a couple of perf traces. The tail looks different depending on where fallback happens — local region fallback to a slower instance causes queueing + kernel switch overhead.

tia: Copying the profiling snippet I grabbed:

```
Profiling (sampled):
- kernel_std (FP16): avg_token 7.2ms p95_token 12ms p99_token 25ms
- kernel_opt (quantized): avg_token 5.4ms p95_token 11ms p99_token 45ms (high variance on cache miss)
- microbatch=1: p95 58ms p99 210ms
- microbatch=4: p95 62ms p99 320ms (queueing tail)
- microbatch=8: p95 130ms p99 340ms
```

alex: Key point: kernel_opt reduces steady-state cost but amplifies single-request tail when KV cache miss forces a full KV load + page faults. The microbatch heuristic is batching aggressively which helps throughput but increases head-of-line blocking for the unlucky request.

maria: How much of the p99 spike is from cross-region fallback vs local cache churn?

kevin: I ran A/B: with routing pinned to local region (no fallback) microbatch=4 p99 dropped from ~320ms -> ~190ms. With fallback enabled during a simulated us-west->eu-west failover p99 jumps back to ~420ms. So fallback is additive to the tail.

jordan: Another observation: when kernel selector switches mid-request (we allowed soft-fallback to a compatible kernel), we pay ~6-12ms penalty plus a scheduler reenqueue that can multiply when multiple requests collide. Not huge alone but material for p99.

tia: KV cache details: when cache hit, token p99 is reasonable. When miss, we do a per-shard fetch and a short memcpy+warmup that can take 30-80ms depending on model size and memory locality. If that coincides with microbatching, those requests end up waiting behind the batch for the load.

alex: So root causes: (1) KV cache miss penalty, (2) kernel switch overhead + scheduler reenqueue, (3) microbatch-induced head-of-line blocking, (4) cross-region added network + cold instance variance.

maria: Proposed immediate mitigations?

kevin: Short list:
- Reduce microbatch cap for latency-sensitive routes (force microbatch<=2) as a config per route.
- Avoid kernel switch during token stream: bind kernel per-request for short-lived requests.
- Eager KV prefetch for large-context requests or warm on placement.
- Routing policy: prefer cold-start-safe instances and avoid cross-region fallback for p99-critical customers.

jordan: Also add a small randomized jitter to batch window to avoid synchronized batching storms that amplify tails.

tia: I can prototype an eager-KV-prefetch: when req header contains recent history size > threshold we pre-warm shards async. Early tests reduced cache-miss tail by ~50%.

sre-bot: Incident-alert: p99 latency > 300ms for model-x in eu-west-1 for 00:11. Logged trace IDs: trace-987, trace-994.

alex: Action items:
- @tia implement prefetch experiment on staging (owner: tia, due: end of week)
- @kevin add per-route microbatch cap and add metrics for 'enqueue-wait-time' (owner: kevin, due: 2d)
- @jordan add kernel-switch telemetry and count reenqueue events (owner: jordan, due: 3d)
- @maria coordinate with infra to tag fallback routes as "latency-sensitive" for a canary (owner: maria, due: 2d)

maria: Also add a perf regression test in CI that simulates cache misses + fallback so we don't regress p99 silently.

kevin: Agreed. I'll sketch the CI test: spawn 200 concurrent single-stream requests, force 15% KV miss, and trigger routing fallback. Expect p99 < 350ms for the latency SLA.

jordan: For long term: consider kernel quality metric that scores p99 variance, not just avg token time, so selector can prefer lower-variance kernels for SLAs.

tia: Noted. I'll include variance in my prefetch experiment logs so we can validate.

alex: Good. Let's keep updates in this thread. If anyone sees a new customer p99 alert, drop it here with trace ids. :thumbsup:
